claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 homogenized at approximately 1200 °C has a high-temperature BCC structure.
The BCC phase of Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is thermodynamically metastable at intermediate temperatures.
Intermediate-temperature aging causes short-range-order clusters to form within the BCC matrix.
The relevant short-range order consists especially of Al–Cr associations.
Formation of Al–Cr short-range-order clusters locally lowers the alloy's free energy.
The local free-energy reduction from short-range ordering compensates for the overall thermodynamic instability of the BCC phase.
Short-range ordering kinetically stabilizes the BCC phase.
This kinetic stabilization delays or suppresses nucleation and growth of equilibrium phases.
Samples aged at 800–1000 °C will exhibit more short-range order than samples immediately quenched from the high-temperature BCC state.
Immediately quenching samples from the high-temperature BCC state produces a baseline with minimal short-range-order development.
Increased short-range order will produce subtle XRD peak shifts indicative of ordering.
Aging-induced short-range order will be accompanied by DSC-detected free-energy reductions.
The extent of short-range-order development will correlate with the degree of BCC phase stability.
The proposed mechanism applies specifically to Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 within the 800–1000 °C regime.
Temperatures outside 800–1000 °C or significant composition changes may introduce competing mechanisms.
